name: Formal Substrate Phase Declaration
purpose: Declare the theorem-preparation phase and freeze the allowed formal-substrate vocabulary before defining mathematical objects.

phase_definition.canonical_statement: The formal substrate phase permits the definition of the minimal mathematical objects, spaces, and relations required for restricted local theorem work within the Mono-Process Framework.
phase_definition.conceptual_foundation: All formal objects are derived from the 'recursively inseparable aspects' breakthrough: meaning is located in the indivisible relation itself.
phase_definition.non_escalation_rule: No formal object or symbolic structure may be treated as final ontology, physical law, or proof of truth.

governance_rules.rule: Every definition must declare its restricted domain and associated failure conditions.
Formal objects must maintain NON_PHYSICAL and ANALOG_ONLY status.
Theorem readiness requires explicit binding of MT targets to substrate objects.
Symbolic structures do not imply physical substrate behavior or ontology identity.

forbidden_claims: The formal substrate proves the framework is 'real'.
Mathematical closure is achieved in this phase.
Substrate objects represent literal physical particles or fields.
